views.cohort_source: H3 Phase I user cohort with identical configuration and seed
views.model_context: full training history, truncated by model maxlen
views.alignment_reference: within-user mean cosine over fixed available genre centroids

attention.reference: non-self raw probability mass minus equal-mass exposure across earlier real keys
attention.position_reference: leave-one-user-out mean conditional attention by lag; cohort-sensitive

methods: Verified-metadata, fractional-genre, post-hoc centroids from frozen learned movie embeddings
Training-only final contextual states, with per-user relative cosine alignment
Actual selected-layer, selected-head last-query causal attention probabilities
Non-self attention mass by genre minus equal-exposure mass from real historical keys
Optional leave-one-user-out, cohort lag-profile reference for position sensitivity
notes: Training-only histories; validation and test events are withheld. Model input remains the full training history, truncated by model maxlen; the selected window changes the comparison profile only.
Every movie splits one unit equally across its genres. All training-seen items are excluded from recommendations.
Age and gender are original MovieLens subgroup attributes; this SASRec implementation takes item sequences and does not use demographic features.
Delta is recommendation share minus historical share; charts express it in percentage points. Each user contributes once to each group/genre estimate.

95% percentile bootstrap intervals resample paired user differences 2,000 times with fixed seeds. No interval is estimated for fewer than two users. Groups below five users are flagged; intervals are not tests of demographic differences.

Unadjusted group means can reflect different input preferences. The optional binned comparison conditions only on the selected genre share in 20-point bins, not full genre profiles, history length, or other confounders. Cells below five users are suppressed in that comparison.
Historical rating distributions are reference profiles, not satisfaction measures. Differences do not establish demographic causation or discrimination.
H3 Phase II inspects actual learned contextual vectors and attention from the final model-visible query position; no demographic labels enter SASRec inference.
Post-hoc genre centroids are not learned genre parameters. Alignment is a within-user-centered cosine difference, not a recommendation probability.

Main attention excess is observed RAW non-self attention probability mass for genre minus uniform-key exposure at the SAME observed non-self mass. Self-attention and padding are excluded from this comparison and reported separately; raw attention is not renormalized.

The optional position reference uses the other users' observed non-self attention by historical lag. It requires support from another user for every lag of the selected user; unsupported comparisons are missing, never zero.

Movies split both genre-reference and attention contribution evenly across their verified genres. Attention effects can reflect sequence position, genre frequency, history composition and other correlated features.
Group means and 95% percentile intervals resample USERS, not individual attention keys. Sparse groups have fewer than five users; uncertainty for fewer than two is unavailable.
Phase I percentage-point changes, alignment differences, and attention excess are distinct quantities and must not be placed on a single numerical scale or interpreted causally.
